tasks.spec:
You are fixing the composite AUDIO timeline in the OBE podcast repo at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. Do NOT git commit, git push, or open a PR. Do NOT send anything externally or publish. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Subscription/OAuth only, zero API spend. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp everywhere. Files you may change: server/pipeline/av_sync.py, server/pipeline/video_assembly.py and tests/test_av_sync.py. You MAY write media into /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite_CANDIDATE.mp4 (that exact path, nothing else under episodes/). Everything else goes in YOUR task directory.

THE OWNER HEARD THIS (Fred E104, 2026-07-25): the two speakers talk over each other, there is dead air, and in a 30-second sample taken at t=60s the GUEST's voice is audible even though he does not join the room until t=224.9s. Four attempts each fixed one property and broke the other; every one of them cost the owner a listen. Do not guess: build a candidate and run the receipt.

TWO PROPERTIES MUST HOLD SIMULTANEOUSLY.
  A. JOIN STAGGER. Each participant's audio must start at their own container start_time. Daily writes one shared session clock: host mic starts at 0.225s, guest mic at 224.875s, host cam 0.229s, guest cam 224.896s. The guest joined ~3.7 minutes late and that silence must be real silence in the mix.
  B. INTERNAL DROPOUTS FILLED. A participant's WebRTC dropouts must become SILENCE of the same duration, never be deleted. The host audio track decodes 2763.5s of content across a 2842s session: about 79s of dropouts. Deleting them slides every later sample earlier, which is what made the speakers drift apart and overlap.

MEASURED BEHAVIOUR OF EACH FORMULATION TRIED (do not repeat these):
  * `asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS` then `adelay(offset)` -- the original. Property A holds. Property B FAILS: it collapses the host's dropouts, his audio ends up 78s early by the end of the session, and the mix runs 2919.6s against 2842.2s of video.
  * `aresample=async=1:first_pts=0` with no adelay -- Property B holds (host track goes 2763s -> 2842s, gaps filled). Property A FAILS: measured in isolation the guest's processed track begins speaking at 1s instead of 224.9s, so first_pts=0 resets him to zero and he speaks ~225s before he joined. Worse, in the assembled mix the host measured +530s displaced.
  * `aresample=async=1:first_pts=0` PLUS `adelay(offset)` -- the guest is shifted twice and lands ~449s.
So `first_pts=0` destroys the stagger and `asetpts` destroys the gaps. You need a formulation that preserves the container timeline INCLUDING its leading offset and its internal holes. Consider (and TEST, do not reason your way to a conclusion): decoding with `-copyts` so absolute timestamps survive into the filter graph; `aresample=async=1` WITHOUT first_pts; `apad`/`atrim` against a known session length; or building each participant's audio by muxing it through the same timestamp-aware path the video already uses successfully. The VIDEO path is correct today and is your reference model: `_normalize_composite_camera` in server/pipeline/video_assembly.py does `setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,fps=30,...` per camera, which resets the start AND holds frames across dropouts, and then the composite pads it to its offset with `tpad`. Video was verified correct on this episode: both speakers' frames land within 0.00s of the map at 500s, 1500s and 2400s with peaks 0.98-0.995.

THE RECEIPT you must satisfy, and which you should run yourself as you iterate:
  COMPOSITE_UNDER_TEST=/mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite_CANDIDATE.mp4 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/podcast-full-auto/composite_audio_check.py
It asserts audio and video lengths agree within 1s, that the host's EARLY content lands at +0s and the guest's content lands at +224.65s (both by cross-correlation against the plainly decoded raw tracks, tolerance 1s), and that the host's late content has not arrived early. It is already validated against two known-bad builds: it fails the shipped composite on the 77.4s length gap, and it fails the async-without-delay build on the host landing +530s off. Building the candidate takes 10-17 minutes through composite_side_by_side, so budget your iterations; you may prototype the audio filter alone with ffmpeg on the four raw tracks in your task directory, which takes under a minute, before committing to a full build.

Build the candidate with the repo's own path: server.pipeline.video_assembly.composite_side_by_side(host_video, guest_video, host_audio, guest_audio, output, offsets=...) where the four raw tracks are the *.webm files under episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/raw sorted by name (index 0 host audio, 1 host video, 2 guest audio, 3 guest video) and the offsets come from server.pipeline.av_sync.offsets_for_paths on those same four paths. Do not hand-write offsets.

Also update tests/test_av_sync.py: keep the existing regression tests that assert the audio stage never uses `asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS` and never re-applies `adelay` on top of absolute timestamps if your formulation still makes those true; if your formulation legitimately needs adelay again, REPLACE those tests with ones that pin your actual contract and explain in the test docstring why the earlier failure mode cannot recur. Never delete a regression test without replacing its guarantee.

VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH and paste the real output into your final message: the receipt command above, and `cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp python3 -m pytest tests/test_av_sync.py tests/test_video_assembly.py -q -p no:cacheprovider`. A claim without executed output is not done. Leave the working tree dirty -- the coordinator lands it.
tasks.verified: A composite built through the repo's own path keeps each speaker at their true join time AND fills their dropouts with silence at the same time, proven by cross-correlation against the plainly decoded raw tracks and by audio and video lengths agreeing within a second
